content: The document outlines the involvement of various experts, organizations, and institutions in the development of guidelines for the treatment of drug-resistant tuberculosis (TB). Below is a professional summary of the key participants and their roles: 1. Dr. José A. Caminero Luna serves as the Coordinator of the MDR-TB Unit at the International Union Against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (UNION) and works at the General Hospital of Gran Canaria “Dr. Negrin” in Las Palmas, Spain. 2. Dr. Sundari Mase is the Medical Team Lead for the Field Services and Evaluation Branch within the Division of Tuberculosis Elimination at the National Center for HIV, Hepatitis, STD, and TB Prevention, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Atlanta, USA. 3. Ms. Lindsay McKenna is a TB/HIV Project Officer at the Treatment Action Group in New York, USA. 4. Dr. Nguyen Viet Nhung is the Director of the National Tuberculosis Control Programme in Hanoi, Vietnam. 5. Dr. Maria Rodriguez coordinates the MDR-TB National Technical Unit at the Ministry of Health in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. 6. Dr. Holger Schünemann (Chair) is a Chair and Professor in the Departments of Clinical Epidemiology & Biostatistics and Medicine at McMaster University, Hamilton, Canada. 7. Dr. James Seddon is a Clinical Lecturer in the Department of Paediatrics at Imperial College London, United Kingdom. 8. Dr. Thomas Shinnick is the Associate Director of Global Laboratory Activities at the Mycobacteriology Laboratory Branch, Division of Tuberculosis Elimination, CDC, Atlanta, USA. 9. Dr. Alena Skrahina is the Scientific Director at the Republican Scientific & Practical Centre for Pulmonology & Tuberculosis in Minsk, Belarus. 10. Dr. J. Peter Cegielski leads the MDR-TB International Programs and Research Branch at the Division of Tuberculosis Elimination, CDC, Atlanta, USA. 11. Mrs. Janet Kristen Ginnard is a Technical Officer in the Strategy & Results Unit at UNITAID, Geneva, Switzerland. 12. Dr. Giovanni Battista Migliori is the Director of the WHO Collaborating Centre for Tuberculosis and Lung Diseases at Fondazione Salvatore Maugeri, Tradate, Italy. 13. Dr. Payam Nahid is a Professor of Medicine at the University of California, San Francisco, and works at the San Francisco General Hospital in the Division of Pulmonary and Critical Care Medicine. 14. Dr. Nobuyuki Nishikiori is a Regional Adviser for TB at the WHO Western Pacific Regional Office in Manila, Philippines. 15. Dr. Thomas W. Piggott is a Resident Physician at McMaster University, Hamilton, Canada. 16. Dr. Anna Scardigli is a Disease Advisor for Tuberculosis at the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria, Geneva, Switzerland. 17. Dr. Barbara Seaworth is a Professor of Medicine and Director of the Heartland National TB Center at the University of Texas Health Science Center, San Antonio, USA. 18. Dr. Mohammed Yassin is a Technical Advisor for Tuberculosis at the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria, Geneva, Switzerland. 19. Dr. Ya Diul Mukadi is a Senior TB Technical Advisor in the Infectious Disease Division of the Global Health Bureau at the US Agency for International Development (USAID), Washington, DC, USA. 20. Dr. Philipp du Cros is a TB Advisor at Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), London, United Kingdom. 21. Dr. Michael L. Rich is a Medical Officer at Partners in Health and Harvard Medical School, Boston, USA. 22. Dr. Abdul Hamid Salim is an Advisor to the National TB Programme in Bangladesh, based in Dhaka. 23. Dr. Valérie Schwoebel is a Medical Officer at the International Union Against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (UNION), Paris, France. 24. Dr. Francis Varaine is the International Medical Coordinator at Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), Paris, France. The document also details the processes for ensuring neutrality and independence in the development of the guidelines. All participants, including members of the Guideline Development Group (GDG), Evidence Review Group (ERG), and external reviewers, were required to submit declarations of interest (DoIs). These declarations were reviewed by the WHO Guideline Steering Committee to identify and manage any potential conflicts of interest. Participants with significant conflicts were excluded from decision-making roles. The guidelines were developed with funding from the United States Agency for International Development (USAID), and the experts contributed their time and expertise to the discussions and reviews. The document emphasizes transparency and adherence to WHO’s conflict of interest policies to maintain the integrity of the guideline development process.
